To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Cape York Welfare Reform Initiative is an example of a program which is designed to help Indigenous Australians to achieve economic and social self‐determination, but that the income management component of the program has been poorly designed, and is likely to be counter‐productive.

CYWR, and in particular CYIM, has been successful in reducing welfare dependency in Cape York communities, and that the success of the initiative has been achieved by a unique combination of factors, including a strong focus on local community consultation and the use of a culturally sensitive, community‐based approach.

the Cape York Welfare Reform initiative, which includes a form of income management, has had mixed success, but that its success has been largely dependent upon the extent to which it has been supported by the local community.
